description:
As a configuration manager, you need to quickly identify changes made to a configuration file. There are two versions of a file: the original configuration file and the modified configuration file. Both files are located in the directory /home/user/configs/ and are named config_v1.conf and config_v2.conf respectively. Your task is to generate a summary file named /home/user/config_changes.log that lists only the lines that have been added in config_v2.conf compared to config_v1.conf. Each added line should appear exactly as it does in config_v2.conf, prefixed by ADDED: (note the space after the colon), and each should be on its own line in the log file. The order of lines in the log file should match their appearance in config_v2.conf. For example, if config_v2.conf contains the added lines server.port=8081 and log.level=debug, then the log file should contain: 
ADDED: server.port=8081
ADDED: log.level=debug
Please ensure that no other lines, prefixes, or content are written to /home/user/config_changes.log. The results must exactly match this format. You do not need to log lines that are deleted or changed; only newly added lines in config_v2.conf compared to config_v1.conf should be included.
truth:
Before the task, the following files exist:

File: /home/user/configs/config_v1.conf
Contents:
server.host=localhost
server.port=8080
database.url=jdbc:mysql://localhost/db
log.level=info

File: /home/user/configs/config_v2.conf
Contents:
server.host=localhost
server.port=8080
database.url=jdbc:mysql://localhost/db
log.level=info
server.port=8081
log.level=debug

After correct completion, the following file will exist:

File: /home/user/config_changes.log
Contents:
ADDED: server.port=8081
ADDED: log.level=debug
